algorithm_description: The algorithm updates x_{k+1} = prox_{eta*g}(x_k - eta * grad(f)(x_k)). Proof must utilize the non-expansiveness of the proximal operator.

evaluator.feedback:
=== CONSENSUS: PASS ===
Mean Completeness: 5.00
Mean Assumption Score: 5.00
Outlier Judges: none

--- judge_0 (openai/gpt-oss-120b, JRS=-0.566) ---
The proof correctly derives the O(1/k) rate (see Theorem T1/T2). Assumption A1 (smoothness and convexity of f) is used in Steps 3, 8 and 11; Assumption A3 (stepsize bound) is used in Step 11. Assumption A2 (non‑expansiveness of the proximal operator) is never invoked, so it is superfluous. The main logical flow is sound, but there are two minor issues: (i) In Step 10 the identity is quoted as \(2\langle a,b\rangle = \|a\|^2+\|b\|^2-\|a-b\|^2\) while the derivation actually uses the equivalent form \(2\langle a,b\rangle = \|a+b\|^2-\|a\|^2-\|b\|^2\). This mismatch should be corrected. (ii) In Step 13 the argument that each term \(F(x_{k+1})-F(x^*)\) is non‑negative is not explicitly justified; a brief comment that \(x^*\) minimizes \(F\) would close the gap. No other gaps or unjustified leaps are present. The proof is otherwise rigorous and complete, but fixing the identity reference and adding the short justification will make it fully polished.

--- judge_1 (meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct, JRS=0.017) ---
The proof is well-structured and easy to follow. All assumptions are clearly stated and used correctly throughout the proof. The convergence rate is correctly derived and matches the stated rate. The special cases are also correctly handled.

--- judge_2 (sarvamai/sarvam-m, JRS=0.017) ---
The proof is methodologically sound and complete. All assumptions are properly invoked in the derivation. The O(1/k) convergence rate is correctly established through telescoping sums and proper application of convexity/smoothness properties. No hallucinations, missing steps, or operator errors detected.
